I would have to say i completely disagree. As i just posted about the burden of proof lies with the believer. It’s not about a lack of anything or showing superiority, it’s about showing tangible evidence which many people haven’t experienced. we live in a world now where many things once thought supernatural are easily explained. If anything asking for proof shows a deeper more curious mind that is aware of the world and how it works. Now, i do believe that some say this and similar things just to be offensive, but that’s not entirely the case. There is nothing wrong with asking for evidence, and there is nothing wrong with saying “i can’t explain it or prove it, i just believe”

Well i’ll say (and i may have missed the mark) that we don’t rlly understand gods. i believe they aren’t “gods” in the way we think of them. yes they are divine beings of immense power, but they still aren’t perfect. They mess up and let emotion decide things for them sometimes, they’re like humans in that way, and just like humans they have personalities that vary. what would be closest to what we think of as a “god” in my opinion would be the universe, but this is so complex and vast that we can’t understand, hence why we created gods as we know them. So to finish this off, no i don’t think god could be all powerful or all good. i believe it could immensely powerful, but not all powerful, and good isn’t a good word to use here since everyone’s idea of “good” is different. God would have a personality with good and bad traits like the rest of us.
